children: Valero Energy

’s VLO investment case is supported by its highly complex coastal refinery network, which can process a wide range of feedstocks into higher-value refined fuels. Concentrated on the Gulf Coast, Valero’s refining network provides another competitive advantage by enabling it to optimize crude sourcing and export the refined products to high-demand markets, supporting margin capture.

Valero’s structural advantage stems from the operational flexibility of its refineries. The company’s system can process a wide range of crude qualities (heavy sour, light/medium sour, etc.) and shift product yields between light products and distillates based on market dynamics to enhance margin capture during volatile times. This is especially beneficial for VLO in the current market environment.

At present, refining capacity around the globe remains constrained due to ongoing disruptions in the Middle East and attacks on Russian refining infrastructure. In its latest earnings call, VLO mentioned that as much as 5 million barrels of global capacity was offline due to these disruptions. VLO’s operational flexibility will enable it to shift product yields toward high-demand, higher-margin products and optimize its crude slate, allowing the company to better capitalize on tighter global refined-product markets.

The structural tightness in the refining market is reflected in elevated refined-product prices, with U.S. average diesel prices recently reaching a record high. Moreover, low global light-product inventories are expected to support refining fundamentals, as inventory normalization could extend well into 2027, keeping margins steady. This prolonged supply-demand imbalance should continue to support refining margins and aid VLO’s profitability.
Other Refining Players to Benefit From Tight Fuel Markets
Par Pacific Holdings

PARR operates an integrated downstream energy business across the United States, with fuel retail operations in Hawaii, Washington and Idaho; refining operations in Hawaii, Wyoming, Washington and Montana; a cumulative refining capacity of 219,000 barrels per day; and a supporting logistics network. Its logistics network includes 13 million barrels of storage, along with marine and pipeline assets for transportation. The commercial flexibility of its downstream network allows the company to capitalize on changing market conditions to support profitability.
PBF Energy

PBF has a geographically diverse refining network with large-scale processing capacity and a highly complex refining system. It operates six refineries — Delaware City Refinery, Paulsboro Refinery, Toledo Refinery, Chalmette Refinery, Torrance Refinery and Martinez Refinery— with a combined throughput capacity of 1 million barrels per day and the ability to process a wide range of feedstocks. The diversified refining footprint provides the company exposure to several regional refining markets, supporting higher margins.
VLO’s Price Performance, Valuation & Estimates
Valero Energy’s shares have jumped 157.7% over the past year compared with the 122.5% improvement of the composite stocks belonging to the industry.
From a valuation standpoint, VLO trades at a trailing 12-month enterprise value to EBITDA (EV/EBITDA) of 8.09X. This is above the broader industry average of 5.78X.
The Zacks Consensus Estimate for VLO’s 2026 earnings has been revised upward over the past seven days.
